value.quote: characterize all the outcomes that can be manipulable by a coalition
value.note: Section 4 estimates shares of manipulable outcomes by Monte Carlo simulation under IAC; exact values are also given for m=3.

C1.reason: Characterising manipulable profiles is about the strategic property, not an axiomatic analysis of rules, so AX does not apply and SB plus SI is correct.

value.quote: the set of all the profiles that are manipulable by it
value.note: All main results concern coalitional misreporting. The sincere profile is used only as the starting point.

C3.1.reason: Every main analysis, including the simulations, concerns profiles at which a coalition misreports, so the code is ALL even though non-coalition voters are sincere within each analysis.

C3.2.reason: Under the codebook, C3.2 is NA when C3.1 = ALL.

C3.3.reason: C3.3 applies only when C3.2 = STATED, which is not the case here.

value.quote_behav: can change their preferences in such a way that this alternative wins
value.quote_info: Notice that it is clearly reasonable for all the members
value.note: Coalition members are strategic in every analysis; non-coalition voters vote sincerely within the same analyses. MIXED (strategic in some analyses, not others) does not fit. Complete knowledge of the profile is only implicit in the coalition coordinating on the exact profile.

C6.VOT.reason: Voters are strategic in every analysis, with sincere non-members in the same analyses, which is not MIXED as the codebook defines it (strategic in some analyses and not others).

value.note: The introduction only reports that Antiplurality is less manipulable. The 'most performing' statement is in Section 4, not in the abstract, introduction or conclusion. The conclusion lists extensions only.

C9.1.reason: The abstract, introduction and conclusion only restate the manipulability results and make no claims about institutions, voters' well-being or which rule should be used.
